findings.finding: AAPOR reports D-margin overstatement of2.7pp across offices in2024, but R overstatement0.6pp in2022 and D overstatement0.1pp in2018. These do not establish a2026 reversal.
findings.model_treatment: Baseline correction zero; estimate separate midterm/chamber error with shrinkage; explicit signed reversal stress only.

findings.finding: Current likely-voter surveys show a Democratic generic-ballot advantage; surveys and aggregate outcomes cannot identify hidden voters or separate switching from composition.
findings.model_treatment: No voter-level or demographic inference; no turnout-to-vote conversion; preserve unknowns.

findings.finding: Recent midterm polling errors were smaller and less consistently directional than presidential-cycle errors.
findings.model_treatment: Fit only earlier midterm cycles and the same office, with matching two-day forecast horizon.

findings.facet: Poll modes, house effects and likely voters
findings.finding: Pollsters use different modes, political weights and likely-voter definitions; low response alone does not determine bias direction.
findings.model_treatment: Retain mode/population metadata; cluster repeat firms/overlapping samples; do not add unsupported mode or house corrections.

findings.finding: Method changes do not guarantee accuracy and shared nonresponse can affect many polls together.
findings.model_treatment: Shared national/state shocks plus race residuals; pollster clustering and uncertainty floors remain explicit sensitivity assumptions.

findings.finding: Marist reports presidential approval40% among likely voters. GDP growth, slower hiring and inflation provide mixed economic context.
findings.model_treatment: Context only: no sufficient matched vintage training series or validated coefficients, so no partisan macro adjustment.

findings.finding: Verified releases cover three Senate contests and NY-17. This small, single-firm seed is not a representative national sample.
findings.model_treatment: Use only direct race polls; no unsupported candidate-quality coefficient, prior district margin or chamber-control odds.

findings.finding: Several states changed2026 congressional boundaries, and some Census products require correction after court decisions.
findings.model_treatment: House inputs require an explicit map vintage. No historical district-number joins or cross-map fundamentals are used.

findings.finding: Kansas and Texas releases provide both initial and leaner versions; these are the same interviews.
findings.model_treatment: Use the initial ballot once, retain undecideds, apply recency decay and shared uncertainty. No forced undecided allocation.

findings.finding: No consistently verified numeric special-election swing or current early-turnout series is included in this snapshot.
findings.model_treatment: Explicitly missing; no zero imputation, preference inference from early turnout, or unrepresentative special-election boost.

findings.finding: The archived pollster-evaluation file ends in2023 overall and selected midterms end in2022; original publication times are absent.
findings.model_treatment: Forward-cycle retrospective diagnostics only, with median-date+7day publication proxy; no claim of vintage replay or2024 validation.

limitations: Partial research seed only:3 Senate races and1 House district, all from one polling firm; no chamber universe or control probabilities.
Probabilities are research scenarios with assumed uncertainty/correlation; they are not a validated complete2026 forecast.
Aggregate data cannot establish who changed votes, whether voters concealed preferences, or why polling errors occur.
No numeric special-election/early-turnout feed, validated macro/local-effect model, official returns reconciliation, or2024 row-level historical data.
Primary publisher facts are attributed extractions; whole copyrighted releases are not redistributed. Source-document SHA256 is unavailable where bytes were not retained.
This is an immutable November1 research snapshot, not a live updating feed.
Historical release dates absent; median field dates, retrospective top-two selection and provider-imputed sample sizes.
CC-BY-4.0; raw bytes, README, license and SHA256 manifest retained under data/elections/sources.
